answer: An operator leases one numbered oil-press. Only that holder may crush a mill-stamped sack of tagged apricot kernels and, at an unannounced bell, tint the first-press oil with a sealed pigment drop so the official sight-glass records a one-shot ripple front whose spectrum must match the lot and the press log. Graders match sack stamp, pigment batch, ripple film, and bell time. A shared press, a leftover sack, or an off-bell tint is slashed as one farm. N aliases cost N exclusive presses, N unique kernel lots, and N live bells no single pressman can staff at once.
